# 1.28.0 — one safety gate for every tool, answer versions, encryption and an audit log

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are.

## One gate for every tool

Until now the chat's own tools went around the protection the agent had: writing a file from the
chat asked nothing and was not checked by SynGuard. Now every tool call — from the chat and from
the agent — passes one gate: the access mode, switched-off tools, hard refusals, SynGuard, your
confirmation, a snapshot for rollback and a line in the audit log.

- **Writing files.** Only a new file in Downloads or on the Desktop is written without a
  question. Overwriting a file, or writing anywhere else, asks first. Anything inside the
  program's own data folder (settings, keys, chats, instructions, the audit log) is refused to
  every tool.
- **Access modes** — the new **Settings → Security** page: *Normal*, *Ask about everything*,
  *Read only* and *Approve everything automatically*. The same page switches individual chat and
  agent tools off; a switched-off tool is not even shown to the model.
- **Allow for a while.** The confirmation window can allow a tool until the end of the reply or
  for the whole chat. PowerShell can only be allowed until the end of the reply.
- **PowerShell is read, not guessed.** A script is now analysed by its syntax tree, and only
  reading runs without a question. The confirmation window lists what the script is going to
  change. Downloads from sites outside the allowlist and account changes that cannot be checked
  are refused with a hint to use the dedicated tool.
- **Hands off the essentials.** Critical Windows processes and services (lsass, csrss, winlogon,
  Windows Defender, the firewall, RPC and more) and the program itself cannot be stopped.
  Browser password and cookie stores, SSH and GPG keys, password vaults, Windows credential
  stores and the SAM/SECURITY hives are not read by any tool.
- **SynGuard failures are visible.** If the safety check could not run or its answer could not be
  read, the tool round says so instead of looking checked.

## Audit log

Every call that changes the system and every refusal is written to an audit log in the profile
folder: time, chat, agent, tool, arguments (secrets removed), outcome, who allowed it and what
SynGuard said. Reading is not logged. The log lives on when chats are deleted, has its own
**Audit** tab in the journal with CSV and JSON export, and travels in the data archive.

## Rollback that really rolls back

- A snapshot now records the registry keys the change touches, value by value. Rolling back
  returns changed values **and removes values and keys added after the snapshot**.
- Services and scheduled tasks are compared with the snapshot and only what differs is touched;
  tasks created during the reply are removed. Startup entries (Run keys) come back too.
- The **Snapshots** tab shows what a rollback will return before you confirm it, lists Windows
  restore points and opens System Restore.
- Re-enabling or disabling a scheduled task during rollback used a wrong command and did nothing;
  fixed.

## Answer versions

**Retry** and editing your question no longer throw away what came after. The previous answer —
with everything that followed it — stays as a version: switch between them with the ‹ 2/3 ›
arrows under the message. Only the version on screen is sent to the model; spending, the journal
and the images of all versions are kept. A version can be deleted on its own.

## Privacy

- **Encrypt conversations on disk** (Settings → Security): chats, the chat list and new audit log
  entries are stored encrypted with Windows' own means (DPAPI) and can only be read under your
  Windows account. Existing chats are rewritten in the background, and both formats always read.
- **Auto-lock** after 5–60 minutes without input, and **Lock now** — for a profile with a
  password. Replies and agent work carry on under the lock screen; the completion notification
  no longer shows the reply's text while locked.
- **Password on the data archive.** Export can protect the `.amrnbak` file with a password
  (AES-256-GCM). A damaged, cut or reshuffled archive is detected, and a wrong password is told
  apart from damage.
- **Delete all data** now works. It asks twice (the second time you type a word), then the
  program restarts and removes the profile's chats, settings, keys, instructions and appearance.
  Other profiles and interface translations stay. The audit log is removed only if you tick the
  box for it.

## Updates

An update is installed only when its SHA-256 checksum is known — from GitHub or from the
`SHA256SUMS` file that now comes with every release — and the file is checked once more right
before it replaces the program, including the step that runs as administrator. A release without
a checksum is never installed by itself; you can still install it with a separate confirmation.
If the program you run is signed, the new version must carry a valid signature of the same
publisher.

## Smaller changes

- **Command line:** `--prompt` now only puts the text into the input field, both on first start
  and when the program is already open. To send it right away, add `--send`. Scripts that relied
  on automatic sending need the new flag.
- **Hotkeys:** a new chat is now **Ctrl+N**; Ctrl+F is free. If you had assigned Ctrl+N to
  something else yourself, your assignment wins.
- **No key yet?** Sending, retrying and continuing now show a notice with a button to
  **Key & Info** instead of a system message box — and Retry no longer erases the answer first.
- **Scheduled tasks** are created only with a known schedule; quotes in a task name are refused.
- **Long repairs:** DISM may run for up to an hour and SFC for 30 minutes, and cancelling the reply
  stops them.
- **English interface:** the confirmation window, agent statuses, sharing, the image viewer, the
  crash window and provider errors are no longer in Russian. The agent writes its explanations
  in the interface language.
- The agent's built-in instructions no longer contain a policy about one particular company's
  software, and its list of commands now names `/agent lite|fast|heavy`. An unchanged saved copy
  of the old instructions is replaced by the new ones.

## File

`Amarin-Admin-AI-v1.28.0-win-x64.exe` — a single file, nothing to unpack, plus `SHA256SUMS` with
its checksum. The file is about 10 MB larger than before: it now carries the PowerShell parser.
